author: Andrew Gregory Health editor
description:
£40m scheme in England aims to keep most vulnerable people well at home and avoid unnecessary hospital stays

Hundreds of thousands of vulnerable patients in England are to receive extra support from their GP as part of a £40m drive aimed at keeping them out of hospital this winter.

As the NHS gears up for the pressures of the coming months, family doctors will offer 300,000 people with frailty and long-term conditions health checks, medication reviews and respiratory tests designed to prevent avoidable hospital admissions.

Continue reading...
title: GPs to offer 300,000 patients extra support to ease winter strain on NHS

author: Sid Lowe at the Riyadh Air Metropolitano
description:
They had been in a battle, they had been behind and they had been on edge, but Barcelona found a way through, holding on to their place at the top of the table and holding the doubts at bay for another day. A fortnight in which they were defeated by Pris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid, in which they might have wondered if something was not quite right, ended with a 2-1 win at Atlético Madrid. This was a proper test, first place awaiting the winner, and in the end that was Hansi Flick’s side.

At a noisy, intense Metropolitano, against an even more intense Atlético, they went behind to a Giuliano Simeone goal and for a while in a frantic first half it looked like there may be no way back. But they found it, two goals from Fermín López either side of half-time lead
title: Barcelona move clear at the top after Fermín López’s double stuns Atlético Madrid

author: Ed Aarons
description:
• Frenchman under pressure after four successive defeats

  • Former Spurs manager Frank emerging as main candidate

Crystal Palace are poised to sack Pierre Sage after Sunday’s defeat by Liverpool left them bottom of the Premier League for the first time since December 2017, with Thomas Frank emerging as the main candidate to succeed him.

The Frenchman, appointed in mid-June to replace Oliver Glasner, has been under mounting pressure since a 5-0 defeat by Brighton last month. There have been few signs of improvement as Palace have slumped to four successive league defeats.

Contin
title: Crystal Palace poised to sack Pierre Sage and target Frank after Liverpool defeat

author: Robert Kitson at Allianz Stadium
description:
• ‘I’m delighted we got the win. He’s a world-class coach’

  • England beat Australia 45-22 in Nations Championship

Maro Itoje, the England captain, has reiterated his squad’s full support for the head coach, Steve Borthwick, after the home side’s resounding 45-22 victory against Australia at Allianz Stadium on Sunday. Itoje described Borthwick as “a world‑class coach” and said England were “lucky to have him” despite fresh media reports of unhappiness in the camp this summer.

Borthwick also revealed he had received several pre-game messages from former England coaches urging him to ignore external criticism and to concentrate on the rugby. His team certainly succeeded in that regard, scoring seven tries to rack up a record number of points against the Wallabies and register only their third win in their past eight games.
title: ‘Lucky to have him’: Maro Itoje backs Borthwick after England triumph

author: Marina Dunbar
description:
Man taken to hospital after falling off Royal Caribbean ship in Pacific Ocean, with Coast Guard investigating incident

A pianist for a Royal Caribbean cruise ship is expected to survive after two Newport Beach, California, fishermen discovered him treading water in the Pacific Ocean nearly 20 miles (32km) offshore on Friday.

The unidentified man was taken to the hospital after the rescue, according to the US Coast Guard, which is now investigating how he went overboard from the cruise ship.

Continue reading...
title: Cruise ship pianist rescued after nine hours treading water miles from shore

author: Graham Searles
description:
Bengals joint-top of AFC North with 34-17 win in Madrid
What do the midterms mean for the NFL? | Email Graham

Broncos 0-0 Panthers 14:56, 1st quarter

Here we go! Carolina kick it away to Denver. The Broncos run it back to the 45-yard line. Nice trot from Sean Fresch. Excellent field position for Bo Nix to go to work.

Continue reading...
title: NFL week nine: Jets v Chiefs, Rams v Commanders, Broncos v Panthers and more – updates

author: Jamie Jackson at Old Trafford
description:
Does this late, late comeback draw keep Michael Carrick in his job? He urged United to back Tuesday’s breathless Roma comeback victory by building momentum and they did – kind of, by avoiding defeat.

Patrick Dorgu’s 96th-minute equaliser went off his head and in: this made it 4-4 to follow Joshua Zirkzee’s own added-time finish as Aston Villa were somehow pulled back by Carrick’s chaotic unit.

Continue reading...
title: Dorgu rescues point for Manchester United in eight-goal thriller against Aston Villa

author: Guardian Staff
description:
The first winter storm began affecting the people of Gaza this weekend with heavy rain hitting on Saturday. Reports that about 70,000 tents were flooded within 12 hours prompted warnings of a worsening humanitarian situation for hundreds of thousands of displaced people living in temporary camps lacking adequate protection from rain and cold

Continue reading...
title: Heavy rain floods displaced families’ tents in Gaza – in pictures

author: Sirin Kale in Kilkenny
description:
Two people arrested after Robinson’s presence inflames tensions in scenes witnessed by many on social media

Two people were arrested at an influencer boxing event that descended into a riot in Ireland after the presence of the far-right activist Tommy Robinson inflamed tensions in the crowd.

The riot took place at about midnight on Saturday at an event organised by the controversial internet personality HSTikkyTokky, whose real name is Harrison Sullivan, at the Hub events venue in Kilkenny.

Continue reading...
title: Riot breaks out at influencer boxing event attended by Tommy Robinson in Ireland

author: Zach Vasquez
description:
SNL booking comedian Druski post-midterms felt misbegotten in low-energy episode failing to capture historic ‘blue-nami’

Four days after the historic “blue-nami” midterms, Saturday Night Live opens at Democrats’ headquarters, where party leaders Hakeem Jeffries (Kenan Thompson) and Chuck Schumer (Sarah Sherman) celebrate, even as they vow to hold on to power in spite of the wishes of their energized base.

Their toast is interrupted by the man responsible for Republicans’ shellacking, Donald Trump (James Austin Johnson). The president, who is “now lame duck”, accepts the results, “which is scarier in a way”. But he’s also resigned to focus on the ballroom, even as he l
title: Saturday Night Live: Druski hosts and James Talarico cameos, but where’s the post-election comedy?

author: Guardian sport and agencies
description:
• Emma Peschel scores on US debut in Group A win

  • Americans outscore opponents 12-0 through two games

  • Sweden bounce back with 4-1 victory over Finland

Emma Peschel celebrated her international debut with a goal as the United States shut out Germany 5-0 at the women’s ice hockey world championship on Sunday.

The 22-year-old defender scored with a wrist shot from the point to make it 2-0 in the opening period of the Group A game.

Continue reading...
title: Peschel scores on debut as USA rout Germany 5-0 at women’s hockey worlds

author: Guardian staff and agencies
description:
Former military chief says prime minister brought Israel to historic crisis and it is approaching ‘point of no return’

Israel’s former military chief Gadi Eisenkot started the tough task of forming a government on Sunday, reaching out to Benjamin Netanyahu’s allies as he said the veteran prime minister had brought the country to a historic crisis.

Eisenkot, 66, the leader of the Yashar party, who has vowed to bridge Israel’s deep polarisation under Netanyahu, formally received a mandate from the president, Isaac Herzog, who gave him 28 days to form a government despite his bloc lacking a clear majority.

Continue reading...
title: Gadi Eisenkot reaches out to Netanyahu allies as he strives to form government

author: Associated Press
description:
President orders prompt investigation after one train derails in collision in al-Ayyat about 30 miles from Cairo

Seven people were killed and more than 100 injured when two trains collided on Sunday south of the Egyptian capital, Cairo, officials said.

The crash occurred in al-Ayyat district in Giza province, about 30 miles south of Cairo, when a train travelling to Fayoum province crashed into the rear of a train heading to the southern province of Aswan, according to the transport ministry.

Continue reading...
title: Collision of two trains in Egypt kills at least seven

author: Reuters
description:
• World No 3 wins 7-6 (5), 7-5

  • Spaniard claims ninth 1000-level title of his career

Carlos Alcaraz avenged his loss to ⁠Ben Shelton in the US Open last eight as he edged the American 7-6 (5), 7-5 to win the Paris Masters ⁠on Sunday, clinching ⁠his ninth ​ATP 1000 title.

The world No 3 controlled the contest from the baseline to become the first Spaniard to win the ⁠tournament since David Ferrer in 2012, while Shelton was left frustrated by an erratic forehand.

Continue reading...
title: Carlos Alcaraz beats error-prone Ben Shelton to win Paris Masters

author: Editorial
description:
The latest vindictive prosecutions and harsh sentences in Hong Kong and Macau are further testimony to China’s ruthless suppression of dissent

One is internationally famous – he was once dubbed “the Face of Protest” by Time magazine – and the other is little known outside his home town. What Joshua Wong and Au Kam San share, beyond the harsh sentences they received last week, is that they represent the spirit of dissent that Beijing is determined to crush.

Mr Wong, who has been in prison for six years, should have walked free next January – not free to fight for Hong Kong’s rights, which China has suppressed so decisively, but at least to walk the streets of the city he loves. Instead, a court last Thursday sentenced the 30-year-old, an
title: The Guardian view on a tale of two activists: Joshua Wong and Au Kam San should not be behind bars | Editorial

author: Editorial
description:
The 225th anniversary of the organisation’s first publication is an opportunity to celebrate its unique contribution to our sense of place

In his one-paragraph short story, On Exactitude in Science, Jorge Luis Borges imagines an empire in which the level of cartographical ambition is so high that a map is made on a one-to-one scale with the imperial territory. The quest for perfect accuracy doesn’t end well. But the earliest map-makers for Ordnance Survey, which this week marked the 225th anniversary of its first publication, might have empathised with the obsessive dedication.

The 1801 OS map of Kent was 10 years in the making, its military-led production inspired by fears of Napoleonic invasion. But as Rachel Hewitt points out in Map of a Nation, her stirr
title: The Guardian view on Ordnance Survey maps: still a superior way to navigate the landscape | Editorial

author: Robert Kitson at Allianz Stadium
description:
• England 45-22 Australia

  • George, Chessum and Heyes scored first-half tries

England had promised to do their talking on the field and so it came to pass. After a turbulent few days, this result was certainly a thumping riposte to newspaper reports that all is not well within the court of Steve Borthwick. If Australia had imagined they might encounter distracted, half-hearted hosts, this seven-try romp suggested the precise opposite.

Maybe Borthwick should commission the Times to write his motivational pre-match speeches every week. On this evidence the ­Wallabies have some massive issues to address but, equally, England were com­fortably the better, more energetic side. Further improvement will still be demanded, of course, but this record number of points against ­Australia was easily their most satisfying all-
title: Henry Pollock powers seven-try England to crushing victory against Australia

author: Nicola Jennings
description: Continue reading...
title: Nicola Jennings on Cop31 in Turkey – cartoon

author: Keren Landman
description:
Med spas are raving about vitamin B12 shots as a pick-me-up. But do they actually make you feel more energized?

If you spend time on social media, you may have seen med spa owners and employees describing vitamin B12 shots as a pick-me-up. When they’re run down or facing a busy week, they say, a quick injection gets them through. Some med spas say many people feel an energy lift within a day or two and recommend a shot every few weeks.

B12 is essential to your health, and people who don’t get enough of it can feel exhausted or worse. But most people already have plenty of B12, and for them, extra doses aren’t likely to help.

Continue reading...
title: Tired all the time? What to know about B12 and if it actually boosts energy levels

author: Sian Cain
description:
Allen, the first live-action film from Pearson’s Ludo Studio, follows a man who met an alien as a kid – and becomes obsessed with bringing him back

  • Get our weekend culture and lifestyle email

If, for whatever reason, you want to feel a bit sad, think too hard about what Elliott from ET would have been like as an adult. Or Coraline, or Matilda, or Chihiro, or those kids in Mary Poppins. The most amazing thing that ever happened in their lives – magic nanny, alien friend, psychic abilities, otherworldly adventures – was already over when they were kids. If that bad Harry Potter play taught us anything, they probably all grew into loser adults.

This is the central premise for Allen, a new Netflix family film by Daley Pearson, co-founder of Ludo Studio, the Brisbane production company
title: Bluey’s Daley Pearson on how losing his brother inspired his new film: ‘He was the best thing ever to me’

author: Hilary Williams as told to Katie Cunningham
description:
Dating as a widow was awkward and I thought a shopping trip would distract me. What it really did was highlight all the couples making homes together

  • Read more in the kindness of strangers series

My wonderful husband passed away in 2010. My father died soon after that, and I remember saying to my mother: “We’re both in the same boat now, Mum – both widowed.” She didn’t agree.

“No, I’m in my 80s and you’ve still got half a life to live,” she responded. “Get out there and live it!”

Continue reading...
title: The kindness of strangers: I was crying on a sofa in Ikea. Then a small gesture reminded me that love is possible

author: Paula Cocozza
description:
Troubled from the age of three, by 35 the American journalist viewed himself as ‘the lowest piece of dirt on the Earth’ – and neither therapy nor drugs seemed to help. But there was one thing he hadn’t tried …

Ted Scheinman can date the origin of his depression with laser accuracy. It was the day he went to the fair, aged three, and returned to his home in upstate New York clutching a Batman toy that he’d won. In the bathroom, he swooped his new doll over the sink. Scheinman had a vivid imagination; in a few years, he would want to become a playwright. To add sound effects and drama, he turned on the tap. There was a whoosh – and the unthinkable happened. Water landed on Batman’s pristine boot in a darkening, enlarging spot that for young Scheinman triggered several rapid thoughts, the last of them being: “I am going to die.”

Now 41, Scheinman, a senior editor at Smithsonian magazine, has written a memoi
title: ‘I was in a darker place than I’d ever been. ECT was my only hope’: how Ted Scheinman finally broke through his depression

author: Emma Beddington
description:
Is it ever OK to leave your family – including small children – to live in the wilderness or walk around the world?

The latest season of Alone – the US TV competition in which cocky survivalists are dropped into a remote, inhospitable wilderness only to be rapidly humbled by squirrels and their own colons – has just ended. I love Alone. The landscapes are spectacular and their implacable hostility to humans obscurely cheering; plus, I get real atavistic satisfaction from watching my favourite contestants make shelters or manage to trap rabbits (grim, but at least every scrap of every creature is usually used – someone even ate a hare’s partially digested stomach contents once). I’m also gripped by what it says about being a man.

Obviously, the contestants aren’t all men, and anyone who goes on a survival show confident they can outlast 11 others living off shrew
title: My ideal man? I’ll take a carer over an adventurer, any day | Emma Beddington

author: Ted Widmer
description:
Tuesday’s winners offered a new politics at a time when ‘there is something broken in America’

As the US election returns came in throughout the night on Tuesday, there was ebullience at the size of the margin. It was comparable to the significant thumpings over the years. Yet bigger.

In 2006, Americans were exhausted by the war in Iraq (by simply changing the last letter to “n”, we have a similar situation today). But even that big win paled in comparison.

Continue reading...
title: ‘The light of dawn is on the horizon’: the best moments from US midterm victory speeches | Ted Widmer

author: Ian Sample Science editor
description:
Benefits of baxdrostat are unexpectedly found to remain up to two years after patients stop taking it

Millions of people with high blood pressure stand to benefit from a new drug that has stunned doctors by reversing a common cause of the condition for years after patients stopped taking the medication.

Patients who took the drug, called baxdrostat, saw their blood pressure improve during a six- to 12-month course of the daily pills, but unexpectedly the benefits remained up to two years later, with some patients no longer on any hypertension drugs and potentially cured of the condition.

Continue reading...
title: New drug could be cure for common cause of high blood pressure

author: Guardian Staff
description:
The Guardian’s picture editors select photographs from around the world

Continue reading...
title: Soweto fashion and a bookshop hit by an earthquake: photos of the weekend

author: Adam Morton in Melbourne, and Fiona Harvey, Oliver Milman and Graham Readfearn in Antalya
description:
High-stakes talks involving 190 countries begin on Monday as world grapples with El Niño supercharged by fossil fuels

The Cop31 summit must produce progress, “a tangible outcome ... that people can see is real”, its host has said as scores of world leaders and representatives of close to 190 countries gather in Turkey for the UN climate talks.

The high-stakes meeting begins on Monday, as countries around the world grapple with the strongest El Niño weather system on record, supercharged by fossil fuels, which is set to take hundreds of thousands of lives and cause damage costing trillions of dollars.
title: Cop31 must deliver climate progress that people can see is real, host says

author: Pippa Neill Environment reporter
description:
Ineos is driving exports with potentially far-reaching environmental and social repercussions

“My children started getting sick,” says Lois Bower-Bjornson, a campaigner at the Clean Air Council in Washington County, Pennsylvania.

“My oldest son had rashes all over his body. His ears, his eyelids, everywhere. My youngest had terrible nosebleeds, it was so bad that he became anaemic and would almost pass out. He would wake up bleeding.”

Continue reading...
title: Revealed: how a UK firm is spearheading growth in trade of US fracked ethane

author: Edward Helmore
description:
The movement founded by Greg Glassman grew into an empire, helping popularize the masculinity aesthetic embraced by Pete Hegseth and RFK Jr

Comparative machismo is hardly new, but when Donald Trump publicly admired Senator Jon Husted’s backside earlier this month, later telling advisers it made the since-defeated Ohio incumbent more “interesting” to voters, the senator leaned into the compliment, saying it gave him extra motivation to “get down to the gym”.

Would that odd exchange have taken place without CrossFit, the fitness empire founded by college dropout and gymnast Greg Glassman in the 1990s that grew to 15,000 gyms across 160 countries before he was drawn into public controversy at the height of #MeToo and the social justice movement in 2020?

Continue reading...
title: How CrossFit helped shape the macho fitness culture of Trump’s America

author: Felicity Cloake
description:
Banana bread is delicious, keeps for ages, goes with all sorts – and it’s thrifty, too! Here’s how to make it in a few easy steps

Banana bread is, strictly speaking, more of a loaf-shaped cake, but, whatever you call it, the taste doesn’t lie. It’s utterly delicious, and the natural sweetness of the ripe fruit lends itself perfectly to baking. While it may not be exactly a health food, it is at least surely better for the heart than Elvis’ favourite fried banana and peanut butter sandwich.

Prep 25 min
Cook 1 hr
Makes 1 loaf

Continue reading...
title: How to make banana bread – recipe | Felicity Cloake's Masterclass

author: Heba Gowayed
description:
The blue wave, while a rebuke of Trump’s policies, was also a referendum on the party’s status quo

On election night I stood in a crowd at Harlem Tavern, a restaurant in New York City, at the electoral party for Darializa Avila Chevalier, the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) member and congresswoman-elect from New York’s 13th congressional district. The crowd cheered as what came to be called the “blunami” rolled in: Iowa blue, Kansas blue, Talarico in Texas, Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan, House, Senate, gubernatorial races overwhelmingly going for the Democratic party.

The victories were a clear rebuke of Trump’s politics, but also a referendum on the Democratic party’s own centrism that is complicit in the violence of masked men hunting immigrants, the funding of a genocide and the denial of healthcare to citizens of the world’s wealthiest country.

Heba Gowayed is an associate professor of sociology at CUNY Hunter College and Graduate Center and author of
title: Centrism did not win the Democratic party the election

author: Chris Stein in Washington
description:
Midterms success gives party potent leverage over Trump – expect tough campaigns of investigating and lawmaking

“Costs, chaos, corruption”: after almost two years spent relentlessly criticizing Donald Trump for failing to address those three, broad political concerns, Democrats won a monumental return to power in Tuesday’s midterm elections that will give them potent new leverage over the president.

Now the question becomes: what will they do with it?

Continue reading...
title: Healthcare, tariffs – but not Trump impeachment: Democrats chart next two years of power

author: Dave Schilling
description:
The once-bearded New York mayor has downsized his facial hair. Does it work?

I’ve battled with facial hair almost my entire adult life.

I started growing it early, turning me into a pubescent villain from a spaghetti western. I was told by my parents not to shave it off, lest it grow back more furious than before. I just had to walk around high school looking like a hungover bond trader, which did nothing for my popularity.

Dave Schilling is a Los Angeles-based writer and humorist

Continue reading...
title: Zohran Mamdani has a mustache now. We cannot take this lightly | Dave Schilling

author: Chris Osuh Community affairs correspondent
description:
See My World, an event highlighting the pan-African thought via film, poetry and dance, builds on momentum sparked by local activists and creatives

African philosophies including exploring how lessons from the past can shape the present and near future have inspired a film festival coming to Manchester.

See My World, a day dedicated to independent creators from across the African diaspora in the north of England, will take place at the Contact theatre on 21 November.

Continue reading...
title: How African philosophies inspired a new approach to staging film festivals in Manchester

author: Steven Strogatz and Alex Townsend
description:
From roundabouts to the stock market, relentless streamlining could be making the world more dangerous

We have all been there: packed shoulder to shoulder on the train while the person beside us coughs and sneezes. A protective flu jab offers some reassurance, but so does the thought that there will be a hospital bed for you, should you need it. Yet, in England, about 95% of adult hospital beds were occupied at the height of flu season last year.

If hospitals were hotels, that level of occupancy would be good business, and we would commend them for their efficiency. But do we really want a hospital to have so few beds in reserve that it’s just one bad flu week away from having to treat patients in corridors?

Continue reading...
title: The efficiency trap: why optimising everything can backfire, badly

author: Angela Giuffrida and agencies
description:
Six people killed in attack probably inspired by far right, according to officials, as police say suspect’s parents and sister found dead at his home

Polish prosecutors have opened a terrorism investigation after a 24-year-old man opened fire in a busy market square in Kraków, killing six people including a Briton and injuring 17, in an attack that authorities said was probably inspired by far-right ideologies.

Police confirmed on Sunday that three people found dead at the gunman’s home after the attack on Saturday afternoon were his father, 53, mother, 52, and sister, 21.

Continue reading...
title: Polish prosecutors open terrorism investigation into Kraków shooting

author: Jack Snape
description:
• Kangaroos beat Toa Samoa 44-12 at Sydney’s Allianz Stadium

  • New Zealand await Australia in next weekend’s men’s final

This was supposed to be Samoa’s chance to challenge the wilting Kangaroos, whose patchy recent performance made them appear vulnerable – to make up for the loss in the last World Cup final, when Australia kept Toa Samoa scoreless for much of that defeat at Old Trafford.

So when the famed Siva Tau, Samoa’s pre-match ritual, brought the Samoans and the Australians close enough to kiss, the anticipation for this semi-final could not have been higher; the match seemed almost certain to explode.

Continue reading...
title: Reece Walsh hat-trick drives Australia past Samoa and into Rugby League World Cup final

author: Fiona Harvey Environment editor
description:
Delegates from more than 190 countries are gathering in Turkey for climate talks, but the US will be absent

As the planet faces unprecedented human-caused global heating, heads of government are meeting for the next fortnight for the latest round of climate talks. We ask why it matters and what is likely to be achieved.

Continue reading...
title: Cop31: what is at stake at the UN climate summit and what can it achieve?

author: Kim Willsher
description:
Luc Corlouër made ‘deal’ with Prix Goncourt winner Philippe Jaenada over his research into model Louise Cansot, murdered in Paris in 1949

For almost eight decades the artists’ model Louise Cansot, the subject of the novel winning France’s most prestigious literary prize this year, was one of Paris’s forgotten murder victims.

After her body was found near the Seine in September 1949, city police wrote off the young woman, immortalised as “the girl of 100 portraits”, as loose, libertine and – worse – an unmarried mother. They closed their investigation after just four months having made little effort to find her killer.

Continue reading...
title: How the story of ‘the girl of 100 portraits’ inspired two books

author: Steven Morris
description:
Margaret Parkes and her husband, in their 80s, want Allan Grimson to reveal location of their son Simon’s remains

The mother of a teenage Royal Navy sailor who vanished 40 years ago has called for a “serial killer” suspected of murdering him to finally reveal where her son’s body is hidden.

Speaking as Simon Parkes’ suspected murderer, the former navy petty officer Allan Grimson, was sentenced for sexual offences against four boys and men, Margaret Parkes, 80, said time was running out for her and her 84-year-old husband, David, to find out what happened to their son.

Continue reading...
title: Mother of Royal Navy sailor missing for 40 years calls for suspected killer to confess

author: Julian Borger
description:
Four pivotal elections in past two weeks show power of grassroots activism to push back against authoritarianism

A sequence of four pivotal elections over the past two weeks in disparate regions of the world has inflicted significant setbacks on authoritarian leaders, and inspired renewed faith that democracy is more resilient than had been feared.

The elections in Brazil, Serbia, Israel and the US were held in widely varying circumstances with unique factors, but each showed the power of grassroots activism to produce surprises that pushed back against would-be autocrats and could perhaps begin to reverse a worldwide drift towards authoritarianism.

Continue reading
title: Election results in Brazil, Serbia, Israel and US renew faith in resilience of democracy

author: Anita Chaudhuri
description:
It’s tempting to ignore uncomfortable feelings – but maybe they’re the key to a happier, more successful future. Time to increase your psychological flexibility …

Something infuriating happened to me recently. My local gym closed down, and overnight what I laughingly call my fitness regime was toast. Quite literally, because now instead of plodding, spinning and lifting tiny dumbbells, I was spending my early mornings guzzling lavishly buttered sourdough.

Obviously, I could have brainstormed alternatives, from going for a run outside or taking an online class to – simple plan – joining one of the five other gyms in my neighbourhood. But instead I chose to see the inconvenience of it all. I grew creakier and crankier by the day.

Continue reading...
title: ‘What is this emotion telling me?’ How anger, fear and jealousy can point the way to a better life

author: Ellen E Jones
description:
Ten years after her landmark political documentary 13th, the film-maker delivers a follow-up on the 14th amendment – and the Trump administration’s attempts to dismantle birthright citizenship

When I ask Ava DuVernay how she kept her focus while making her new film – or how anyone does, when the onslaught of news, fake news and disputed facts seems designed to overwhelm – she starts to answer, then stops. Her eyes have filled with tears.

“I just got emotional, as you said that, because it was the film that saved me,” she says. “It’s been a very tough two years. I live in Los Angeles, and I’ve seen people in my neighbourhood pulled out of their cars. The lady who sells flowers next to my office was there one day, and the next day she wasn’t. People I know personally are literally hiding in their houses, like Anne Frank vibes … So when I would feel the rage and the fear, I put it into the film … And I just … I was doing something.”
title: ‘I’ve seen people in my neighbourhood pulled out of their cars’: Ava DuVernay on the cruelty and brutality of Trump’s America

author: As told to Rich Pelley
description:
The singer lives by the words of John Lennon, and once did karaoke surrounded by supermodels. But which song still makes him cry?

The first song I fell in love with
I first heard Bob Dylan through my cousin David when I was about 16. I fell in love with his voice. Don’t Think Twice, It’s All Right is still one of the best songs ever written. We were young rebels then, looking for a moral compass, while everybody older seemed to be wearing bowler hats and pinstripe suits. Dylan made us think differently.

The song I inexplicably know every lyric to
Astral Weeks by Van Morrison. I’m going to record it myself some time because it’s just an amazing song.

Continue reading...
title: ‘My dad said Great Balls of Fire was pagan music – and threw it out of the window’: Leo Sayer’s honest playlist

author: Facundo Iglesia in Buenos Aires
description:
President has opposing views on many issues, and once called Leo’s predecessor the ‘representative of the Evil One’

Trees are being planted in the garden. The brightly coloured buildings are getting another coat of paint. The choir rehearses. Hundreds of other residents, several of them using wheelchairs, practise their positions outside the sanctuary. Excitement is in the air, because on Monday 9 November, the Cottolengo Don Orione – a Catholic-run home for disabled people – will be the first stop on Pope Leo XIV’s first full day of his trip to Argentina.

But the pope’s visit to Claypole, about 26km from Buenos Aires, does not come at an especially happy time for the home, which counts about 400 residents with disabilities. Argentina’s president, Javier Milei, has made wide-ranging cuts to disability funding.

Continue reading...
title: Pope’s visit to Argentina sets up showdown with ‘hyper-capitalist’ Milei

author: Jack Snape
description:
• Church scores four tries as Australia beat Fiji Bulikula 30-14

  • Jillaroos will face New Zealand in the final next weekend

The Jillaroos survived an almighty scare from Fiji in the World Cup semi-final, securing a place in the tournament decider against New Zealand at Lang Park next week despite a stunning resistance from the brilliant Bulikula.

Driven by the exquisite, unpredictable playmaker Luisa Yaranamua – 23 and yet to play an NRLW match – and supported by powerful, committed teammates, Fiji led for much of the first half and were level with the Jillaroos at half-time.

Continue reading...
title: Abbi Church powers Australia to win over spirited Fiji as hosts reach Women’s Rugby League World Cup final

author: Ellie Violet Bramley
description:
Event regarded as Oscars of fashion industry replaces John Galliano retrospective with homage to the ‘extra ordinary’

A few months after the planned John Galliano Met Gala retrospective was cancelled amid a backlash focused on the designer’s past, a more commonplace theme has been announced: “extraORDINARY: fashion and the poetics of the everyday.” It has left some commentators speculating that celebrities might replace the couture “omelette dresses” and four-part red-carpet performances with jeans and a nice top.

While the dress code for the next Met Gala, which will be held on 3 May 2027, is yet to be announced, it traditionally derives from the exhibition theme.
title: From the overblown to the ordinary? Met Gala 2027 to celebrate ‘poetics of everyday’

author: Rhiannon Lucy Cosslett
description:
Prescriptions for these beta blockers are soaring among England’s teenage girls. But they deserve more than this sticking-plaster approach

The first time I had a panic attack, I genuinely thought I was dying. Unless you have experienced one, it is hard to understand just how physical the symptoms can be – the pounding heart, the shortness of breath, the dizziness, the chest pain, the nausea. When they became frequent, I would often have to go to bed to sleep them off, my body utterly spent from the strain of sheer, corporeal terror. A panic attack is not a physical state that I would wish on anyone. It is pure fight or flight.

Like many others, I was prescribed a drug called propranolol to help with my anxiety symptoms. Propranolol is a beta blocker used in cardiac patients to lower the heart rate, but it is increasingly prescribed to
title: There is no ‘magic pill’ to fix young women’s anxiety. I should know – I once took propranolol myself | Rhiannon Lucy Cosslett

author: Anjali Doshi
description:
I have reported on cricket for two decades. The abuse I have been subjected to in recent years is shocking and demoralising

By Wisden Cricket Monthly

Twenty-four years ago I walked into the Wankhede press box for the first time, to cover an India v England one-day international. That sultry Mumbai evening, Andrew Flintoff sprinted across the outfield twirling his shirt round his head as England won by five runs – a sight that so annoyed captain Sourav Ganguly that he would take his revenge on the Lord’s balcony later that summer.

I wrote my report for a local tabloid, the Afternoon Despatch & Courier, with trepidation and an overwhelming sense of impostor syndrome. I was one of only two women among the contingent, and was terrified about what my male peers and senior colleagues would make of my presence and work.
title: Female sports journalists have always faced sexism. Social media has made it vicious and relentless | Anjali Doshi

author: Sarah Butler
description:
Farmers face big drop in production from extreme weather during this year’s super El Niño event

Banana producers in Latin America are calling for better pay to help cope with the impact of the climate crisis, as they face big drops in production resulting from extreme weather during this year’s super El Niño event.

High winds in parts of Colombia, one of the biggest suppliers to the UK market where droughts are predicted in some regions this year, and heavy rainfall in Peru and Ecuador are already affecting production, according to the Fairtrade Foundation ethical trade body. In the Dominican Republic, farmers are expected to face drought conditions, with forecasts of drier and warmer than usual conditions.

Continue reading...
title: Banana producers in Latin America want better pay to cope with effects of climate crisis

author: Rupert Jones
description:
Emails claim to come from a woman whose husband has died – but the offer isn’t what it seems

An email pops up in your inbox: a woman whose husband has died is giving away his grand piano for free. She says she would love it to go to someone “who will truly appreciate and care for it”. The piano “is in excellent condition and has brought joy to our home”.

The email ends: “If you know of a dedicated student, teacher, family or church that would cherish this piano, please feel free to forward this message to them.”

Continue reading...
title: ‘Free grand piano’: the scam playing on music lovers’ heartstrings

author: Jonnie Bayfield
description:
Former loggers and poachers have embraced ancient traditions to promote and protect the Cardamom Mountains’ ever-threatened natural wonders

I’m two hours downriver from the Chi Phat community ecotourism camp, in the Koh Kong region of Cambodia, when my phone signal fizzles out completely. It’s dawn and we’re chugging through the snaking Preak Piphot River towards the starting point of a 9-mile (15km) overnight trek into the country’s sacred, spirit-filled Cardamom mountain range. The region, a six-hour bus ride west of the capital Phnom Penh, recently made global news for being home to a raft of
title: Walking with spirits in Cambodia’s sacred forests

author: Sammy Gecsoyler
description:
David Lammy among those raising concerns after errors found in rejected applications for indefinite leave to remain

Concerns have been raised over the sudden rise in number of Turkish nationals facing removal from the UK as a result of mistakes, prompting accusations that the Home Office has failed to learn the lessons of the Windrush scandal.

Since the start of the year, there has been a sharp rise in the number of rejected applications for indefinite leave to remain for those on European Community Association Agreement (ECAA) visas, a longstanding route to residency for Turkish nationals seeking to set up a business in the UK.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Windrush’ accusations over sharp rise in Turkish nationals facing removal from UK

author: Rebecca Ratcliffe, Gloria Dickie and Elisângela Mendonça
description:
Mumbai facility is part of Reliance Industries, owner of world’s biggest oil refinery and funder of controversial mega-zoo

The Prince of Wales’s Earthshot prize will host its forthcoming annual awards ceremony at a venue owned by the billionaire Ambani family conglomerate, drawing criticism from conservationists over their fossil fuel businesses and their foundation’s controversial mega-zoo.

A spokesperson for the Earthshot prize, which awards £1m to five winners every year to invest in conservation work, confirmed to the Guardian and the news outlet Mongabay that this year’s ceremony will be held at the Jio World Convention Centre in Mumbai on 17 November.
title: Environmentalists criticise choice of Earthshot prize venue owned by fossil fuel firm

author: Dan Milmo and Aisha Down
description:
As AI exposes flaws in IT systems and geopolitics plays out on the cyber frontline, some experts say the events of recent weeks could soon be a common occurrence

Alex Pearce was doing the morning rounds at his fruit and vegetable wholesale business in London on Monday last week when he noticed something odd.

The defrost light on refrigeration unit 2 was on, and the panel reading was 150C. Unit 4 was the same.

Continue reading...
title: Hot fridges, a fake nuclear alert and a $6bn heist: are we in the foothills of a hacking epidemic?

author: Annalisa Barbieri
description:
You haven’t formed strong friendships since relocating, but that takes time and returning home will have its own costs – not all of them financial

My husband and I are in a dilemma about where to live. We are in our early 30s and have an 18-month-old daughter. We are from the East Midlands but moved to the north-west three years ago to buy our first house. Our parents are in the East Midlands, as well as a few friends. My brother, who I am close to, also plans to move back from London in the next few years.

We moved to have a change, and for my husband to have some distance from our parents. He is not that close to his; I am close
title: Should we move back closer to family before our daughter starts school? | Ask Annalisa Barbieri

author: Simon Hattenstone
description:
The legendary country singer says he did everything wrong. Yet now, at 93, he’s music’s last man standing. What’s the secret of his longevity?

• Read an exclusive extract from Willie Nelson’s memoir here

Before the interview, Willie Nelson’s publicist warns me that there’s only one thing the 93-year-old country music legend doesn’t like to discuss: the past. Which rules out talking about the 150-plus albums he’s made; the Highwaymen, the supergroup he formed with Kris Kristofferson, Johnny Cash and Waylon Jennings; writing On the Road Again on an aeroplane sick bag. It also rules out talking about paying off a $32m tax bill with a double album called The IRS Tapes; co-founding Farm Aid with Neil Young and John Mellencamp; taking $40,000 off Woody Harrelson in a single poker session; or breaking up a massive brawl in a parking lot with two Colt 45s before signing
title: Willie Nelson: ‘I drank too much, I smoked too much. I took too many pills’

author: Simon Tisdall
description:
With the global tide turning against him, the US president’s lame duck status could still aggravate old tensions and spark new explosions

It was a victory for the world, too. People in the many countries that suffered pain, loss and cruel indignities at the hands of Donald Trump over the past two chaotic, fearful years celebrated a moment of glorious, shared redemption. The monster, like others of his kind, still lurks in his gilded White House lair; far-right authoritarianism still casts a dark shadow over many nations. But the power of this most destructive of presidents is shattered, his malignant spell broken. The triumphant roar of US midterm voters was a rallying cry of democratic defiance that, echoing the American revolution of 250 years ago, reverberated around the globe.

For Iranians, Trump’s electoral humiliation raised hopes, perhaps misplaced
title: Donald Trump’s power is on the wane. What next for Russia, Israel – and the rest of us?  | Simon Tisdall

author: Peter Beaumont Senior international correspondent
description:
In a war driven by drones and battlefield sensors, access to space is essential. After Starlink speed restrictions and Russian Oreshnik missile strikes, Kyiv is racing to develop its own space capabilities

For people in the Russian industrial city of Samara on the banks of the Volga, the first they knew of the Ukrainian attack were detonations that sent a column of smoke into the air.

If the Kremlin was vague about the target, video footage on social media soon made it clear what had been hit in the early hours of 15 August: the Progress Rocket and Space Centre, manufacturer of Russia’s Soyuz-2 rockets.

Continue reading...
title: Ukraine’s new frontier: how space has become critical to balance of the war

author: Amy Hawkins
description:
Activists fear Bangkok will give in to pressure from Beijing despite reports of torture and human rights abuses against the mostly muslim ethnic minority

The deportation of two more Uyghurs to China from Thailand would put their lives in grave danger, activists have said, with one of the men saying he would be “like a slave” if he was sent back.

Last year, Thai authorities forcibly deported 40 Uyghur men to China despite pleas from the men themselves and the UN.

The US and Canada had reportedly offered to resettle them, but Bangkok appeared to want to avoid upsetting Beijing. The
title: Uyghurs facing deportation by Thailand say they will be ‘like slaves’ in China

author: Robert Mackey
description:
White says he has meeting with Trump in Washington DC on Monday, without saying whether he will accept the job

Donald Trump has offered the job of White House press secretary to Dana White, the chief executive of the Ultimate Fighting Championship, the president said in a social media post on Saturday.

Trump described White, who staged a cage-fighting spectacle at the White House to mark the president’s 80th birthday in June, as “a violent Fighter and Warrior”, credentials unlike any ever used to describe previous press secretaries.

Continue reading...
title: Trump says he asked Dana White, UFC boss, to be his new White House press secretary
